speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities in more detail, and when did it first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of a facial rash sparing the perioral area is a classic sign often referred to as "slapped cheek," which strongly suggests Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. To confirm this clinical suspicion, I need to verify if the trunk rash has a lacy or reticular pattern and if there are any joint pains. Does the rash on your body look like a lacy or net-like pattern, and have you experienced any joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lacy, reticular pattern of the trunk rash combined with the classic "slapped cheek" facial rash and preceding viral symptoms confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
